topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecturer, contextualises the cancer lecture series, and establishes the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Causes of Cancer and Epidemiological Variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures in driving population-level cancer incidence.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, illustrated through the discovery and molecular etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Direct and Metabolically Activated Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical compounds undergo endogenous processing to form DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Vulnerability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how non-mutagenic environmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Assessing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro screening strategies used to evaluate whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Risk Assessment and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture by evaluating practical risk-benefit trade-offs in environmental exposures and summarising core takeaways.
